subject: Unable to load R library (ggplot2) in RApache

messages.author: faa5427c06a1e034
messages.subject: Unable to load R library (ggplot2) in RApache
parts:
Hi

I am getting error:

From directive REvalOnStartup on line 17 of /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf.
Error in library(ggplot2) : there is no package called 'ggplot2'

I have installed ggplot2 package after RApache has been built. Do I need to rebuild RApache if I install R packages after rapache is built?

If not could you please guide me why RApache is not able to locate ggplot2 package. I can load this package successfully through R terminal.

Regards
Santosh

messages.author: faa5427c06a1e034
messages.subject: Re: Unable to load R library (ggplot2) in RApache
parts:
The issue is resolved:

Somehow the package was not installed properly, the main reason was that the directory where the packages get stored was not having write permission. I changed the permission (chmod 777) and then re-insatlled ggplot2 package (install.packages). It is now working fine, producing the ggplot2 plot.

Notes: (my observations/ experiments):

1. Loading the library can be done either in httpd.conf or within the .R script. Both works..
2. To produce ggplot, you need to store the plot in a variable and then print the plot (I also read this in some other thread), otherwise it does not work. For me it give errors like the one below when I was not printing the plot:

In file(con, "rb") :
  cannot open file '/tmp/file4713293ce989': No such file or directory

For reference find below the code to plot a simple bar plot:

library("ggplot2")
setContentType("image/png")
t <- tempfile()
df <- data.frame(time = factor(c("Lunch","Dinner"), levels=c("Lunch","Dinner")), total_bill = c(14.89, 17.23))
png(t,type="cairo")
# stote the plot
gg=ggplot(data=df, aes(x=time, y=total_bill)) + geom_bar()
# print the plot
print(gg)
dev.off()
sendBin(readBin(t,'raw',n=file.info(t)$size))
unlink(t)
DONE

Regards
Santosh Marigowda

messages.author: 48f24841e806e6c6
messages.subject: Re: Unable to load R library (ggplot2) in RApache
parts:
On startup, rapache behaves a bit differently than R:

rApache doesn't source profiles of any kind, neither site nor user. R does. Implication being a reduced library path, so that's why users report rapache not finding a library when user installs it from command line R.

rApache's working directory is typically a place where the web server cannot write files, so it is up to the user to manage where files are stored. users should also not presume the working directory they set will be set on each web request.

rapache processes share one temporary directory, so its important that users create unique file names.

Jeff
